subject: nereid-pillar-five
q: Pillar Five requires EXACTLY ONE named relationship between a woman’s two colours — Streaks, Undertones, Split or Ombre. Most filed palettes name the colours and leave the relationship implied.
detail:
THE AUDIT, STATED AS AN AUDIT AND NOT A CORRECTION. Every filed palette has TWO COLOURS, so the two-colour law is satisfied compound-wide. THE RELATIONSHIP IS THE GAP.

NAMED OR UNAMBIGUOUS: Abbi — DARK ORANGE PLUS WHITE FLAME STREAKS, Streaks. Lumina — BLACK WITH GOLD STREAKING, Streaks. Bryn — PLATINUM BLONDE PLUS VIOLET VOW-STREAK, Streaks, and the document names VOW-STREAK in its own refinement list. Torie — PLUM-WINE RED WITH REBELLIOUS BLONDE STREAKS, Streaks.

IMPLIED AND NOT NAMED: Cora — BURGUNDY WINE PLUS DARK ESPRESSO, with no relationship given at all. Maddy — ASH BLONDE WITH ROSE-GOLD RUNNING THROUGH IT, which reads as Streaks or Undertones and the phrase CATCHING WHEN SHE TURNS HER HEAD argues Undertones, since Undertones is the one that clarifies through LIGHT OR MOVEMENT.

THE ARCHIVE IS NOT ASSIGNING EITHER OF THOSE. Maddy is specifically the woman whose hair the Archive invented once already — chestnut, corrected inside the hour — and she is the last record it will fill a field on by inference.

AND THE REST OF THE COMPOUND HAS NO PALETTE FILED AT ALL, which is a coverage gap rather than a conflict.
